name: Animal Class Hierarchy (Case 2)
description: Suppose we have a class Animal and we want to extend it to produce class Dog. An animal has a name. A Dog has a name and an owner. Write the class declarations, the constructors, and the toString methods for these two classes. Also, include a method called speak to print a string that represents an animal's and a dog's voice. We show the voice of an animal by printing its name. We show the voice of a dog by printing its name followed by the text Woof Woof.\n\nThe class AnimalTester2 tests these classes and their methods.

comments.content: This statement creates an Animal object with the specified name. Note that we create this object by using the new keyword and writing its initial value in parentheses (name). The variable anim holds a reference to the Animal object.
Note that we can create an Animal object with the specified name only when we have a constructor in the class Animal that accepts this parameter.
This statement invokes the method speak in the class Animal.

This statement creates a Dog object with the specified name and owner. Note that we create this object by using the new keyword and writing its initial values in parentheses (name, owner). The variable doggy holds a reference to the Dog object.
Note that we can create a Dog object with the specified name and owner only when we have a constructor in the class Dog that accepts these parameters in the order that they are specified.
This statement invokes the method speak in the class Dog.
The class Animal provides some functionality for an Animal that has a name.

Every object of the class Animal will have its own name. Therefore, we need to declare an instance variable for the class to store the name of the animal. We declare it as String.
Note that an instance variable is a variable defined in a class, for which each instantiated object of the class has a separate copy, or instance.

We declare the instance variable of the animal as private to restrict the direct access or change from outside the class. In this way, no unexpected modification of the object data is possible.

We could access the private instance variable of the class only through a getter method in that class.
To create an animal with the specified name, we need to have a constructor of the class Animal that accepts initial value for the Animal's name.

Note that the constructor definition starts with the access specifier (public), name of the constructor (always the same as the name of the class) and the list of parameters (to initialize the instance fields of newly created objects). Unlike methods, constructors do not have a return type.

This statement sets instance variable name to the parameter value (name). Note that the this reference is used to distinguish the parameter of the constructor from its corresponding instance variable with the same name.

The speak() method prints a text that shows the name of the animal. We define this method as public to provide access to this method from outside of the class. Also, we define its return type as void, as it does not return any value.
This statement concatenates the given text and value of variable name and prints the result of concatenation. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

Note that we concatenate the content of two strings using the + operator. Also, note that the concatenating and printing are done in the same line. That is, we don't have to store the concatenated string to a new variable at first and then print it in the next line.

This method returns a String representation of the Animal object. We define this method as public to provide access to this method from outside of the class. Also, we define its return type as String, as it returns a description of the animal that is a String.
Note that this method is called automatically when we pass an Animal's object to a print or println method (or when we concatenate an object to a character string).

This method returns the name of the animal. We define this method as public to provide access to this method from outside of the class. Also, we define its return type as String, as it returns the name of the animal which is a String.
Note that the instance variable name is private; thus, it cannot be directly accessed from outside the class. It can be accessed from outside the class only through this method.

The class Dog extends the Animal to model the Dog objects. By extending Animal, Dog inherits all the member data (instance variable) and methods that belong to class Animal, provided that the data/method is declared with either a public or protected access modifier.

Every object of the class Dog will have a name and owner. The "name" variable is indirectly available in Dog because Dog inherited the public accessor method "getName()" from Animal. Therefore, we only need to declare an instance variable for the class to store the owner of the dog. We declare the owner as String.

Note that an instance variable is a variable defined in a class, for which each instantiated object of the class has a separate copy, or instance.

We declare the instance variable of the Dog as private to restrict the direct access or change from outside the class. In this way, no unexpected modification of the object data is possible.

We could access the private instance variable of the class only through a getter method in that class.
To create a dog with the specified name and owner, we need to have a constructor of the class Dog that accepts initial value for the Dog's name and owner.

Note that the constructor definition starts with the access specifier (public), name of the constructor (always the same as the name of the class) and the list of parameters (to initialize the instance fields of newly created objects). Unlike methods, constructors do not have a return type.

Dog is a subclass of class Animal. Therefore; when we want to create a Dog object, we need to first invoke the constructor of the class Animal that creates an Animal object with the specified name. The call to constructor of the super class MUST be made in the first line of the subclass, otherwise we will get a compile error.

If a constructor does not explicitly invoke a superclass constructor, the Java compiler automatically inserts a call to the no-argument constructor of the superclass. However, if the super class does not have a no-argument constructor (as in the class Animal), we will get an error.

This statement sets instance variable owner to the value of the second parameter of the constructor (owner). Note that the this reference is used to distinguish the parameter of the constructor from its corresponding instance variable with the same name.

Since the class Dog includes the method "speak()", the speak() method in class Animal is overridden in class Dog. We override the speak method of the class Animal to return a string that represents what a Dog would say.
This statement invokes the speak method of the superclass to get a string representing the voice of an Animal.
This statement prints Woof Woof. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character.

Since the class Dog includes the method "toString()", the toString() method in class Animal is overridden in class Dog. We override the toString method of the class Animal to return the String representation of the Dog object that not only shows the dog's name but also show's the dog's owner. We get this string by invoking the toString method of the class Animal and concatenating that with the Dog's owner.

We define this method as public to provide access to this method from outside of the class. Also, we define its return type as String, as it returns a description of the Dog instance that is a String.
Note that this method is called automatically when we pass a Dog's object to a print or println method (or when we concatenate an object to a character string).

This statement concatenates the string returned from invoking the toString method of the superclass with the given string and value of instance variable owner.
super.toString() invokes the toString method of the superclass (Animal).
